```ts
import { MEASURES, type DecisionStatement, type MeasureKind, type ReversalKind, type RuleId, type StandingBasis } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { statementParagraphs } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { DecisionMessage } from "../auth";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { beginMailRecord, lockPendingAuthorMail, recordAuthorMail, type MailState } from "./repo";
import { endedMeasures, endedStanding, repliedTo, statementActions, statementDecision, type StatementDecisionRow } from "./statement-repo";

/**
 * The data a statement of reasons and its mail are rendered from (3c design, sections 7.5 and 10). A decision is the
 * statement: every element is a column, a ledger row or a saved text, read here into the one shape that @korbat/rules
 * renders for the mail, the author's screen and the console's preview. Nothing read here is changed by a later event, so
 * a statement reads as it was sent whenever it is rendered.
 */

/** A decision's statement with what mailing it needs: whom it is about, and whether its mail is still owed. */
export interface StatementFound {
  statement: DecisionStatement;
  decision: StatementDecisionRow;
}

/** Whether a field reset's old value was still kept when the decision that ends or lifts it was made, and where it can be read. */
function resetFacts(kind: MeasureKind | ReversalKind, held: { decisionId: string; ruleId: string | null; noEffect: string | null; snapshotKept: boolean }) {
  const target = MEASURES[kind].target;
  if (target !== "display_name" && target !== "bio") return { resetDecisionId: null, oldValueKept: false, resetRuleId: null };
  // The reset's own snapshot holds the old value, by its compare-and-set; a reset that changed nothing removed none.
  return { resetDecisionId: held.decisionId, oldValueKept: held.noEffect === null && held.snapshotKept, resetRuleId: held.ruleId as RuleId | null };
}

/** The statement's data of one decision, or null when no decision has the id. */
export async function decisionStatement(q: ModerationDeps["apiDb"], decisionId: string): Promise<StatementFound | null> {
  const decision = await statementDecision(q, decisionId);
  if (!decision) return null;
  const actions = await statementActions(q, decisionId);
  const ended = decision.kind === "final" ? await endedMeasures(q, decisionId) : [];
  // 3e: the standing measures whose basis a reversal of this decision broke; absent from a statement that holds none.
  const brokenBasis = decision.kind === "review" || decision.kind === "correction" ? await endedStanding(q, decisionId) : [];
  // 3e Task 4: the reply this correction or review answered by keeping or reversing its measure; absent when none.
  const replied = decision.kind === "review" || decision.kind === "correction" ? await repliedTo(q, decisionId) : null;
  // The facts and the reason are told with a decision that restricts (it holds a measure), with a correction and with a
  // review. Those of a decision without a measure are the case's record, for staff: such a decision tells its author at
  // most that what korbat did while deciding has ended, so the statement's data holds neither, and no mail, screen or
  // export that is rendered from it can carry them.
  const told = decision.kind === "correction" || decision.kind === "review" || actions.some((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts === null);
  const statement: DecisionStatement = {
    kind: decision.kind,
    outcome: decision.outcome as DecisionStatement["outcome"],
    ground: decision.ground as DecisionStatement["ground"],
    ruleId: decision.ruleId as RuleId | null,
    rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
    redressVersion: decision.redressVersion,
    legalReference: decision.legalReference,
    facts: told ? decision.facts : null,
    reason: told ? decision.reason : null,
    source: decision.source as DecisionStatement["source"],
    decidedAt: decision.decidedAt,
    post: decision.targetType === "post" && decision.postCreatedAt !== null ? { id: decision.targetId, createdAt: decision.postCreatedAt } : null,
    measures: actions
      .filter((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts === null)
      .map((action) => ({
        kind: action.kind as MeasureKind,
        mediaId: action.mediaId,
        noEffect: action.noEffect,
        sealed: action.kind === "seal_media" ? { posts: action.sealedPosts, images: action.sealedImages, deletedImages: action.sealedDeletedImages } : null,
        // 3e: what the ledger fixed for good about a strike, a standing measure and a retirement, so its statement reads as
        // it was sent (a retirement's sentence reads its end from whether the decision suspends or terminates at once).
        ...(action.kind === "strike" ? { endsAt: action.endsAt, activeThen: action.activeThen } : {}),
        ...(action.kind === "suspend" || action.kind === "terminate"
          ? {
              announced: action.announced,
              days: action.days,
              basis: action.basis as StandingBasis | null,
              earliestStart: action.earliestStart,
              endsAt: action.endsAt,
              restsOn: action.restsOn === null ? null : action.restsOn.map((entry) => ({ ...entry, ruleId: entry.ruleId as RuleId | null })),
            }
          : {}),
        ...(action.kind === "retire_handle" ? { handle: action.handle, placeholder: action.placeholder } : {}),
      })),
    reversals: actions
      .filter((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts !== null)
      .map((action) => ({
        kind: action.kind as ReversalKind,
        mediaId: action.mediaId,
        ...(action.lifted === null ? { resetDecisionId: null, oldValueKept: false, resetRuleId: null } : resetFacts(action.kind, action.lifted)),
        // 3e: the handle a reversal of a retirement gives back.
        ...(action.kind === "unretire_handle" ? { handle: action.handle } : {}),
        // 3e: what a lift of a suspension lifted, where its period stood then, and whether it was a withdrawal for another measure.
        ...(action.kind === "lift_suspension"
          ? { liftedKind: action.liftedKind, liftedDecidedAt: action.liftedDecidedAt, periodThen: action.periodThen, replaced: action.replaced, replyFiledAt: action.replyFiledAt }
          : {}),
      })),
    endedMeasures: ended.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind as MeasureKind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, ...resetFacts(measure.kind, measure) })),
    ...(brokenBasis.length > 0 ? { endedStanding: brokenBasis } : {}),
    ...(replied !== null ? { repliedTo: replied } : {}),
    reviewed:
      decision.reviewed === null
        ? null
        : {
            kind: decision.reviewed.kind,
            ground: decision.reviewed.ground as DecisionStatement["ground"],
            ruleId: decision.reviewed.ruleId as RuleId | null,
            // The reviewed decision's own rulebook version: its rule is rendered as it was worded when that decision was made.
            rulesVersion: decision.reviewed.rulesVersion,
            legalReference: decision.reviewed.legalReference,
            decidedAt: decision.reviewed.decidedAt,
          },
  };
  return { statement, decision };
}

/**
 * The subject of the statement's mail, by the decision's kind and outcome (3c design, section 7.15), as a key of the mail
 * template's own table: a seal first, whatever else the decision holds; then a decision taken while deciding, on a post
 * or on an account; a final restriction; a final decision that restricts nothing but ends or lifts what was done while
 * deciding, and a correction of a decision taken while deciding; a reversal of a final decision; and a kept appeal.
 */
export function mailSubjectOf(statement: DecisionStatement): Extract<DecisionMessage, { template: "moderation_decision" }>["subject"] {
  const seals = statement.measures.some((measure) => measure.kind === "seal_media");
  const post = statement.post !== null;
  if (statement.kind === "interim") return seals ? "seal_deciding" : post ? "post_deciding" : "profile_deciding";
  if (statement.kind === "final") {
    if (seals) return "seal_final";
    if (statement.outcome === "restricted") return post ? "post_restricted" : "profile_restricted";
    return "lifted_deciding";
  }
  if (statement.kind === "correction") return statement.reviewed?.kind === "interim" ? "lifted_deciding" : "reversed";
  return statement.outcome === "kept" ? "appeal_kept" : "reversed";
}

/**
 * The template a decision's statement is mailed under (3e design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6): the first row of 7.15's
 * table that fits, and moderation_decision otherwise, so that a strike, a retirement and their reversals ride on 3c's
 * mail. In order: an announced suspension or termination; one taken at once; the answer to a reply (a statement with
 * `repliedTo`); a lift of one (a withdrawal signed `replaced` under its own lead), or a decision whose reversal ended one by
 * breaking its basis. The reporting measures join with the task that builds them.
 */
export function mailTemplateOf(statement: DecisionStatement, paragraphs: readonly string[]): DecisionMessage {
  const standing = statement.measures.find((measure) => measure.kind === "suspend" || measure.kind === "terminate");
  if (statement.kind === "final" && standing !== undefined && standing.announced === true) {
    const measure = standing.kind === "terminate" ? "terminate" : "suspend";
    if (standing.earliestStart === undefined || standing.earliestStart === null) throw new Error("an announced measure's mail names its earliest start: the statement's data holds none");
    // The window is the row's own: its earliest start less its decision's time, in hours.
    const window = Math.round((Date.parse(standing.earliestStart) - Date.parse(statement.decidedAt)) / 3_600_000);
    return { template: "suspension_announced", measure, days: measure === "terminate" ? null : (standing.days ?? null), window, earliestStart: standing.earliestStart, paragraphs };
  }
  if (statement.kind === "final" && standing !== undefined && standing.announced === false) {
    const measure = standing.kind === "terminate" ? "terminate" : "suspend";
    return { template: "suspension_started_at_once", measure, days: standing.days ?? null, endsAt: standing.endsAt ?? null, paragraphs };
  }
  const lift = statement.reversals.find((reversal) => reversal.kind === "lift_suspension");
  if (statement.repliedTo !== undefined) {
    // A review that reverses part but leaves the measure in force answers the reply as a kept answer does.
    const lifted = lift !== undefined && lift.replaced !== true;
    return { template: "reply_answered", outcome: lifted ? "reversed" : "kept", paragraphs };
  }
  if ((statement.kind === "review" || statement.kind === "correction") && lift !== undefined && lift.replaced === true && lift.liftedDecidedAt) {
    return {
      template: "suspension_lifted",
      measure: lift.liftedKind === "terminate" ? "terminate" : "suspend",
      why: "replaced",
      decidedAt: lift.liftedDecidedAt,
      replied: lift.replyFiledAt !== undefined && lift.replyFiledAt !== null,
      paragraphs,
    };
  }
  if ((statement.kind === "review" || statement.kind === "correction") && lift !== undefined && lift.periodThen) {
    return { template: "suspension_lifted", measure: lift.liftedKind === "terminate" ? "terminate" : "suspend", why: "lifted", period: lift.periodThen.state, paragraphs };
  }
  const broken = (statement.endedStanding ?? []).find((entry) => entry.kind === "suspend" || entry.kind === "terminate");
  if (broken !== undefined) return { template: "suspension_lifted", measure: broken.kind === "terminate" ? "terminate" : "suspend", why: "basis", period: broken.periodThen.state, paragraphs };
  return { template: "moderation_decision", subject: mailSubjectOf(statement), paragraphs };
}

/**
 * Mails a decision's statement to its author when that mail is still owed, and records what became of it: `sent`,
 * `no_address` for an account that is gone, `failed` when the relay refused the address for good. A failure of the relay
 * is thrown, and the mail stays pending for the dispatch job. Answers what was recorded, or "none" when nothing was owed.
 *
 * The decision's row is taken before the mail is sent, in the transaction that records the result (beginMailRecord): a
 * database that cannot write refuses that, and nothing is sent, so a mail is never sent again and again for want of a
 * record. Two senders of one statement (the decision's own request and the dispatch job) then send it once: the second
 * waits for the row and finds the mail recorded.
 *
 * 3e (design, section 5, the lock order, item 4): for a decision that holds an announced suspension or termination, the
 * outcome fixes the measure's start (the database's decisions_mail_standing derives the profile's columns), so the
 * transaction takes the subject's profile FOR NO KEY UPDATE first and the decision's row after it, as a deciding
 * transaction takes the profile before it touches decisions.
 */
export async function sendStatement(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "social">, decisionId: string): Promise<MailState | "none"> {
  const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, decisionId);
  if (!found || found.decision.authorMail !== "pending") return "none";
  const subject = found.decision.subjectId;
  // The statement is rendered before anything is sent: one that cannot be rendered is no mail, and stays pending.
  const message = mailTemplateOf(found.statement, statementParagraphs(found.statement));
  const announced = found.statement.kind === "final" && found.statement.measures.some((measure) => (measure.kind === "suspend" || measure.kind === "terminate") && measure.announced === true);
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await beginMailRecord(tx);
    if (announced && subject !== null) await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [subject], "no key update");
    if (!(await lockPendingAuthorMail(tx, decisionId))) return "none";
    const result = subject === null ? "no_address" : await deps.auth.mailAccount(subject, message);
    // A stop of the address never holds a statement back, so "suppressed" is never answered for it.
    const state: MailState = result === "sent" ? "sent" : result === "refused" ? "failed" : "no_address";
    await recordAuthorMail(tx, decisionId, state);
    return state;
  });
}
```

```ts
import { Readable } from "node:stream";
import { AppealsQuery, FindingRequest, MEDIA_SIZES, MediaId, QueueQuery, StaffTextSaveRequest } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono, type Context } from "hono";
import { z } from "zod";
import { AuthError, type ActiveStaffSession, type AuthForStaff, type StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { validate } from "../lib/validate";
import type { ModerationForStaff } from "../moderation";

/** A case's id in a path, in the lower case the database writes: a read finds the case by value whatever the spelling. */
const CaseId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());
const CaseParam = z.object({ case: CaseId });
const ImageParam = z.object({ case: CaseId, media: MediaId, size: z.enum(MEDIA_SIZES) });

/**
 * The console's case routes (3c design, sections 5 and 7), a route group the staff routes mount behind the staff gate.
 * Each stands behind requireStaff; one that changes something a user sees, or that cannot be undone, stands behind
 * requireStaffStepUp as well, which verifies the key's confirmation of exactly what the route is about to do. Three
 * writing routes stand without it, by name: saving a text, taking a fresh snapshot and opening a finding. None of them
 * changes anything a user sees, and each enters the record only through a confirmed decision that names its digest or
 * its case. The handlers only call the moderation module's staff interface and shape the answer: the step-up stays the
 * auth module's, the cases the moderation module's.
 */
export function caseRoutes(auth: AuthForStaff, moderation: ModerationForStaff) {
  const routes = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  /** The session requireStaff read; a route without it in front is a wiring fault, not a refusal. */
  const staffSession = (c: Context<AppEnv>): ActiveStaffSession => {
    const session = c.get("staffSession");
    if (!session) throw new Error("a staff route ran without requireStaff");
    return session;
  };

  /** The confirmation requireStaffStepUp verified; a route without it in front is a wiring fault, not a refusal. */
  const confirmedStepUp = (c: Context<AppEnv>): StaffStepUpConfirmed => {
    const confirmed = c.get("staffStepUp");
    if (!confirmed) throw new Error("a staff route that changes something ran without requireStaffStepUp");
    return confirmed;
  };

  // The home screen's numbers, the same for every staff member but one: how many appeals this person may review.
  routes.get("/overview", auth.requireStaff, async (c) => c.json(await moderation.overview(staffSession(c))));

  // Open cases by lane and age. The console refreshes it without the activity mark.
  routes.get("/queue", auth.requireStaff, validate("query", QueueQuery), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.queue(c.req.valid("query").cursor)));

  // 3e: the Standing screen's four lists, read only: no list is a queue key, and people are handles.
  routes.get("/standing", auth.requireStaff, async (c) => c.json(await moderation.standing()));

  // A moderator's own finding opens a case, or joins the target's open one: a named exception to the step-up.
  routes.post("/findings", auth.requireStaff, validate("json", FindingRequest), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.openFinding(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("json")), 201));

  // The case. Every read is written to the access log and held to the day's limit on different cases.
  routes.get("/cases/:case", auth.requireStaff, validate("param", CaseParam), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.caseView(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("param").case)));

  // An image of the case's post, on the console's own origin: the only way an image reaches the console. The moderation
  // module answers a file only when the image may be shown to staff at all and is this case's; every refusal is one 404.
  // Never stored anywhere, and always WebP, whatever the bytes are: the store's files are checked before they are
  // handed over, and nosniff with the API's own policy keeps them inert. A HEAD request never gets here: the staff group
  // answers it before any route, so no file is opened and no view logged for a request that shows nothing.
  routes.get("/cases/:case/media/:media/:size", auth.requireStaff, validate("param", ImageParam), async (c) => {
    const { case: caseId, media, size } = c.req.valid("param");
    const file = await moderation.caseImage(staffSession(c), caseId, media, size);
    c.header("Cache-Control", "private, no-store");
    c.header("Content-Type", "image/webp");
    c.header("Content-Length", String(file.size));
    // The stream closes the handle when it ends or fails.
    return c.body(Readable.toWeb(file.handle.createReadStream()) as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>);
  });

  // A fresh snapshot of the case's target as it stands: a named exception to the step-up. It answers an id and a digest,
  // never content, so every read of a case's content goes through the case's own route.
  routes.post("/cases/:case/snapshots", auth.requireStaff, validate("param", CaseParam), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.takeSnapshot(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("param").case)));

  // Saving a text: a named exception to the step-up. The text enters the record only when a confirmed decision or reveal
  // names its digest; a note and a recorded choice not to seal are complete when saved.
  routes.post("/cases/:case/texts", auth.requireStaff, validate("param", CaseParam), validate("json", StaffTextSaveRequest), async (c) =>
    c.json(await moderation.saveText(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("param").case, c.req.valid("json")), 201),
  );
  // The person's own drafts on the case, with their salts.
  routes.get("/cases/:case/texts", auth.requireStaff, validate("param", CaseParam), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.texts(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("param").case)));

  // A decision on a case: the path's case is the action's target, and the body is the action's params with the assertion
  // as `stepUp`. The decision commits with its audit row or not at all. When the confirming key or account no longer
  // opens anything by then, the session that confirmed has ended, and requireStaff clears both cookies on that answer as
  // on its own; when the challenge's time ran out, the console asks for the key again. The answer is the case as it now
  // stands, so the console shows what the decision left; the case is the one the step-up confirmed.
  routes.post(
    "/cases/:case/decisions",
    auth.requireStaff,
    auth.requireStaffStepUp("case_decided", (c) => c.req.param("case")),
    async (c) => {
      const outcome = await moderation.decide(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c), { requestId: c.get("requestId") });
      if (outcome === "ended") throw new AuthError("staff_session_required", 401);
      if (outcome === "late") throw new AuthError("challenge_expired", 400);
      return c.json(await moderation.decidedCase(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c).target.id), 201);
    },
  );

  // The pending appeals, newest first, each marked whether this person may review it. No row carries the appellant's
  // statement: it is read on the case page, whose read is logged and counted.
  routes.get("/appeals", auth.requireStaff, validate("query", AppealsQuery), async (c) => c.json(await moderation.appeals(staffSession(c), c.req.valid("query").cursor)));

  // The review of an appeal: the path's decision is the action's target (the decision that was appealed), and the body
  // is the action's params with the assertion as `stepUp`. The review commits with its audit row or not at all, and an
  // ended confirmation and a late one answer as a decision's do. The answer is the decision's case as it now stands.
  routes.post(
    "/decisions/:decision/review",
    auth.requireStaff,
    auth.requireStaffStepUp("appeals_reviewed", (c) => c.req.param("decision")),
    async (c) => {
      const outcome = await moderation.review(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c), { requestId: c.get("requestId") });
      if (outcome === "ended") throw new AuthError("staff_session_required", 401);
      if (outcome === "late") throw new AuthError("challenge_expired", 400);
      return c.json(await moderation.reviewedCase(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c).target.id), 201);
    },
  );

  // Who sent an item: the path's item is the action's target, and the body is the reason's category and the digest of
  // the saved reason, with the assertion as `stepUp`. The access row and the audit row commit together or not at all, and
  // the identity is read only after that commit. An ended confirmation and a late one answer as a decision's do.
  routes.post(
    "/items/:item/reveal",
    auth.requireStaff,
    auth.requireStaffStepUp("identity_revealed", (c) => c.req.param("item")),
    async (c) => {
      const outcome = await moderation.reveal(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c), { requestId: c.get("requestId") });
      if (outcome === "ended") throw new AuthError("staff_session_required", 401);
      if (outcome === "late") throw new AuthError("challenge_expired", 400);
      return c.json(outcome);
    },
  );

  return routes;
}
```

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from "react";
import { Platform, ScrollView, Text, View, type TextInput } from "react-native";
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS, BadgeVerifyResponse, DeleteStartResponse, EmailChangeResponse, FlowResponse, type MeResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { ReauthPanel, ReenrollNotice, useReauth } from "@/components/security/ReauthPanel";
import { SettingsNav } from "@/components/SettingsNav";
import { Body, Button, ErrorText, Field, Loading, Notice, Section } from "@/components/ui";
import { api, ApiError, apiResponse, errorMessage } from "@/lib/api";
import { exportFilename, saveBlob } from "@/lib/download";
import { useSession } from "@/lib/session";
import { STANDING_TEXTS } from "@/lib/standing";

type Run = (action: () => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>;
type Refresh = () => Promise<unknown>;

/**
 * Expo inlines this public value into the web bundle at export time (WEB_BADGE in infra/.env). The
 * badge routes answer badge_unavailable when the API's verification provider is off, and there is no
 * harmless read to probe that with, so the section is shown only by a build that says "on"; the API's
 * provider is off by default, and so is this.
 */
const BADGE_SHOWN = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE === "on";

const CODE = /^\d{6}$/;

/** One request at a time for a section, through the re-authentication hook, with its busy, error and done texts. */
function useAction(run: Run, describe: (err: unknown) => string = errorMessage) {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [done, setDone] = useState<string | null>(null);
  // Enter in a field calls the action as the button does, so the button's busy rule is here too: a second Enter while a request is out sends nothing.
  async function act(action: () => Promise<void>) {
    if (busy) return;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    setDone(null);
    try {
      await run(action);
    } catch (err) {
      setError(describe(err));
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }
  return { busy, error, setError, done, setDone, act };
}

/**
 * Moves the focus to `target` when `away` turns false after being true: the section went back to the
 * step `target` is in, and the control that had the focus (Start over, Cancel, Change, Verify, Remove
 * badge) left the tree with the step it was in, which would drop the focus to the page body.
 */
function useFocusOnReturn(away: boolean, target: RefObject<{ focus(): void } | null>) {
  const wasAway = useRef(away);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!away && wasAway.current) target.current?.focus();
    wasAway.current = away;
  }, [away, target]);
}

/** A new address gets a code; the account moves to it once the code is entered, and every session stays signed in. */
function EmailSection({ me, run, refresh }: { me: MeResponse; run: Run; refresh: Refresh }) {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [flowId, setFlowId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const { busy, error, setError, done, setDone, act } = useAction(run);
  const emailRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);
  // The code field takes the focus itself (autoFocus); Change and Start over bring the address field back, which takes it here.
  useFocusOnReturn(flowId !== null, emailRef);
  // The API would answer a generic invalid_request for the account's own address; it is refused here in its own words instead.
  const current = email.trim().toLowerCase() === me.user.email.toLowerCase();

  // Enter in the field calls this as the button does, so the button's conditions come first.
  async function start() {
    if (email.trim().length === 0) return;
    if (current) {
      setDone(null);
      setError("That is already your email address.");
      return;
    }
    await act(async () => {
      const flow = await api("/api/auth/email/change/start", { json: { email: email.trim() }, schema: FlowResponse });
      setCode("");
      setFlowId(flow.flowId);
    });
  }

  async function verify() {
    if (!CODE.test(code.trim())) return;
    await act(async () => {
      const changed = await api("/api/auth/email/change/verify", { json: { flowId, code: code.trim() }, schema: EmailChangeResponse });
      setFlowId(null);
      setEmail("");
      setCode("");
      setDone(`Your email address is now ${changed.email}.`);
      // The address shown here and on the security screen reads the session.
      await refresh();
    });
  }

  return (
    <View>
      <Body>Your address is {me.user.email}. Sign-in codes and security messages go there, and nobody else sees it.</Body>
      {flowId ? (
        <>
          <Body>We sent a code to {email.trim()}. Enter it to move your account to that address. Every session stays signed in.</Body>
          <Field label="Code from the email" autoFocus autoComplete="one-time-code" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={6} value={code} onChangeText={setCode} onSubmitEditing={() => void verify()} />
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Button label="Change" onPress={() => void verify()} busy={busy} disabled={!CODE.test(code.trim())} />
          <Button
            label="Start over"
            onPress={() => {
              setFlowId(null);
              setCode("");
            }}
            tone="secondary"
          />
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <Field ref={emailRef} label="New email address" autoComplete="email" autoCapitalize="none" inputMode="email" value={email} onChangeText={setEmail} onSubmitEditing={() => void start()} />
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Notice message={done} />
          <Button label="Send code" onPress={() => void start()} busy={busy} disabled={email.trim().length === 0 || current} />
        </>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** The API reuses the email flows' code errors, whose wording points at an email; the badge's code came by text message. */
function badgeMessage(err: unknown): string {
  if (err instanceof ApiError && err.code === "invalid_code") return "That code is not right. Check the text message.";
  if (err instanceof ApiError && err.code === "code_expired") return "That code has expired. Send a new one.";
  return errorMessage(err);
}

/** Holding the badge, verifying a number, or removing it; each needs fresh authentication. */
function BadgeSection({ me, run, refresh }: { me: MeResponse; run: Run; refresh: Refresh }) {
  const [phone, setPhone] = useState("");
  const [flowId, setFlowId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const { busy, error, done, setDone, act } = useAction(run, badgeMessage);
  const verified = me.profile?.verified === true;
  const phoneRef = useRef<TextInput>(null);
  const removeRef = useRef<View>(null);
  // The code field takes the focus itself (autoFocus). Start over and a removed badge bring the phone field back, and a verified
  // badge brings Remove badge: each takes the focus when its step returns.
  useFocusOnReturn(verified || flowId !== null, phoneRef);
  useFocusOnReturn(!verified, removeRef);

  // Enter in the field calls this as the button does, so the button's condition comes first.
  async function start() {
    if (phone.trim().length === 0) return;
    await act(async () => {
      const flow = await api("/api/auth/badge/start", { json: { phone: phone.trim() }, schema: FlowResponse });
      setCode("");
      setFlowId(flow.flowId);
    });
  }

  async function verify() {
    if (!CODE.test(code.trim())) return;
    await act(async () => {
      await api("/api/auth/badge/verify", { json: { flowId, code: code.trim() }, schema: BadgeVerifyResponse });
      setFlowId(null);
      setPhone("");
      setCode("");
      setDone("Your account is now verified.");
      // The chip on posts and the profile, and this section, read the session.
      await refresh();
    });
  }

  const remove = () =>
    act(async () => {
      await api("/api/auth/badge", { method: "DELETE" });
      setDone("The badge was removed.");
      await refresh();
    });

  return (
    <View>
      <Body>
        The Verified badge means you hold a phone number that no other account uses. To check it, the number is handed to the verification provider for one text message; korbat
        keeps it only as a keyed hash, never the number itself.
      </Body>
      {verified ? (
        <>
          <Body>Your account holds the badge.</Body>
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Notice message={done} />
          <Button ref={removeRef} label="Remove badge" onPress={() => void remove()} busy={busy} tone="danger" />
        </>
      ) : flowId ? (
        <>
          <Body>We texted a code to {phone.trim()}.</Body>
          <Field label="Code from the text message" autoFocus autoComplete="one-time-code" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={6} value={code} onChangeText={setCode} onSubmitEditing={() => void verify()} />
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Button label="Verify" onPress={() => void verify()} busy={busy} disabled={!CODE.test(code.trim())} />
          <Button
            label="Start over"
            onPress={() => {
              setFlowId(null);
              setCode("");
            }}
            tone="secondary"
          />
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <Field ref={phoneRef} label="Phone number" autoComplete="tel" inputMode="tel" placeholder="+447911123456" value={phone} onChangeText={setPhone} onSubmitEditing={() => void start()} />
          <Text className="mt-1 text-xs text-zinc-400">International format: a plus sign, the country code and the number, without the leading zero.</Text>
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Notice message={done} />
          <Button label="Send code" onPress={() => void start()} busy={busy} disabled={phone.trim().length === 0} />
        </>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** The export's own words for its daily limit: the generic "wait a moment" would be wrong for a window of a day. */
export function exportMessage(err: unknown): string {
  if (err instanceof ApiError && err.code === "rate_limited" && err.retryAfter) {
    const hours = Math.ceil(err.retryAfter / 3600);
    return hours <= 1 ? "You exported your data today already. You can export again in about an hour." : `You exported your data today already. You can export again in about ${hours} hours.`;
  }
  return errorMessage(err);
}

/**
 * The ZIP comes back as the response body, so the raw response is turned into a file the browser saves;
 * native has no downloads folder to offer. The API fails the body when the archive breaks off part way,
 * so res.blob() rejects and the section shows an error, never the note that the export was downloaded.
 */
function ExportSection({ run }: { run: Run }) {
  const { busy, error, done, setDone, act } = useAction(run, exportMessage);

  const download = () =>
    act(async () => {
      const res = await apiResponse("/api/account/export", { method: "POST" });
      saveBlob(await res.blob(), exportFilename(res.headers.get("content-disposition")));
      setDone("Your export was downloaded.");
    });

  return (
    <View>
      <Body>
        The archive is a ZIP with export.json (your account, profile, posts, likes, reposts, bookmarks, follows, blocks, mutes, sessions, devices and security events) and every
        image you uploaded. It holds your email address, so keep it somewhere private. You can export once a day.
      </Body>
      {Platform.OS === "web" ? (
        <>
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Notice message={done} />
          <Button label="Download my data" onPress={() => void download()} busy={busy} />
        </>
      ) : (
        <Body>Export your data from the web app.</Body>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** Deletion needs an emailed code and the handle typed back; the API takes the account down at once and this session with it. */
function DeleteSection({ me, run, refresh }: { me: MeResponse; run: Run; refresh: Refresh }) {
  const [flowId, setFlowId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [typed, setTyped] = useState("");
  const { busy, error, act } = useAction(run);
  const handle = me.profile?.handle ?? "";
  const typedHandle = typed.trim().replace(/^@/, "").toLowerCase();
  // The API compares the typed handle case-insensitively and answers a mismatch as a generic invalid request; the same rule here keeps the button off until it matches.
  const matches = typedHandle.length > 0 && typedHandle === handle.toLowerCase();
  const sendRef = useRef<View>(null);
  // The code field takes the focus itself (autoFocus); Cancel brings "Send me a code" back, which takes it here.
  useFocusOnReturn(flowId !== null, sendRef);

  const start = () =>
    act(async () => {
      const flow = await api("/api/account/delete/start", { method: "POST", schema: DeleteStartResponse });
      setCode("");
      setTyped("");
      setFlowId(flow.flowId);
    });

  // The button's condition comes first, as in every other action of this screen.
  async function confirm() {
    if (!CODE.test(code.trim()) || !matches) return;
    await act(async () => {
      await api("/api/account/delete/confirm", { json: { flowId, code: code.trim(), handle: typedHandle } });
      // The API cleared the cookies: the session reloads as signed out, and the home page is public.
      await refresh();
      router.replace("/");
    });
  }

  return (
    <View>
      <Body>
        {ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS} Your likes, reposts, bookmarks, follows, blocks and mutes are removed too. Your handle stays reserved, so nobody can take it. This
        cannot be undone.
      </Body>
      {flowId ? (
        <>
          <Body>We emailed a code to {me.user.email}.</Body>
          <Field label="Code from the email" autoFocus autoComplete="one-time-code" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={6} value={code} onChangeText={setCode} />
          <Field label="Type your handle to confirm" autoCapitalize="none" autoComplete="off" placeholder={`@${handle}`} value={typed} onChangeText={setTyped} />
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Button label="Delete my account" onPress={() => void confirm()} busy={busy} disabled={!CODE.test(code.trim()) || !matches} tone="danger" />
          <Button
            label="Cancel"
            onPress={() => {
              setFlowId(null);
              setCode("");
              setTyped("");
            }}
            tone="secondary"
          />
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <ErrorText message={error} />
          <Button ref={sendRef} label="Send me a code" onPress={() => void start()} busy={busy} tone="secondary" />
        </>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

export default function AccountSettings() {
  const { state, refresh } = useSession();
  const reauth = useReauth();

  if (state.status !== "signed-in") return <Loading />;
  const { me } = state;

  return (
    <AppShell>
      <ScrollView className="flex-1 bg-zinc-950" contentContainerClassName="px-4 py-6">
        <Text accessibilityRole="header" className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-zinc-50">
          Account
        </Text>
        <Text className="mt-2 text-base text-zinc-400">@{me.profile?.handle}</Text>
        <SettingsNav current="account" />

        {reauth.pending ? <ReauthPanel me={me} pending={reauth.pending} onClose={reauth.clear} /> : null}
        {/* After a recovery code confirmed an action here: the screen stays, with the field for the code it mailed, and says where two-factor is set up again. */}
        <ReenrollNotice me={me} />

        <Section title="Email address">
          <EmailSection me={me} run={reauth.run} refresh={refresh} />
        </Section>
        {BADGE_SHOWN ? (
          <Section title="Verified badge">
            <BadgeSection me={me} run={reauth.run} refresh={refresh} />
          </Section>
        ) : null}
        <Section title="Data export">
          <ExportSection run={reauth.run} />
        </Section>
        <Section title="Delete account">
          {/* 3e Task 4 (design, section 9.2): [terminate.delete], while /me carries a termination. */}
          {me.standing?.measure?.kind === "terminate" ? <Body>{STANDING_TEXTS.terminateDelete}</Body> : null}
          <DeleteSection me={me} run={reauth.run} refresh={refresh} />
        </Section>
      </ScrollView>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Pressable, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { Link } from "expo-router";
import type { AccountStanding } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { bannerSentences, STANDING_TEXTS } from "@/lib/standing";

/** One of the banner's buttons: a link to the screen where the person acts. */
function BannerLink({ label, href }: { label: string; href: string }) {
  return (
    <Link href={href} asChild>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" className="mr-2 mt-3 rounded-lg border border-zinc-500 px-3 py-2">
        <Text className="text-sm font-semibold text-zinc-50">{label}</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </Link>
  );
}

/**
 * The banner above every signed-in screen while /me's standing holds a measure (3e design, section 9.1). It cannot be
 * dismissed, so a deadline is never out of sight. It is a region labelled "Your account's standing" whose first sentence
 * is a level-2 header; amber (a start not fixed, announced, held by a reply) and red (running) repeat what the words say
 * and are never the only signal. Its buttons, each while it applies: Read the decision, Reply (while no reply was sent),
 * Appeal (on the decision's screen, while the appeal is open), Export my data and Delete account.
 */
export function StandingBanner({ standing }: { standing: AccountStanding | null }) {
  const measure = standing?.measure ?? null;
  const sentences = bannerSentences(standing);
  if (measure === null || sentences === null) return null;
  const [first, ...rest] = sentences;
  const decision = `/settings/cases/${measure.decisionId}`;
  const tone = measure.state === "running" ? "border-red-800 bg-red-950" : "border-amber-700 bg-amber-950";
  return (
    <View role="region" aria-label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.label} className={`border-b px-4 py-3 ${tone}`}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" aria-level={2} className="text-base leading-6 text-zinc-50">
        {first}
      </Text>
      {rest.map((sentence) => (
        <Text key={sentence} className="mt-2 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-50">
          {sentence}
        </Text>
      ))}
      <View className="flex-row flex-wrap">
        <BannerLink label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.read} href={decision} />
        {measure.replyOpen ? <BannerLink label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.reply} href={`${decision}/reply`} /> : null}
        {measure.appealUntil !== null && !measure.appealPending ? <BannerLink label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.appeal} href={decision} /> : null}
        <BannerLink label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.export} href="/settings/account" />
        <BannerLink label={STANDING_TEXTS.banner.delete} href="/settings/account" />
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}
```

```tsx
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {

      setBusy(false);

export function DecisionDetail({ view, onAppeal }: { view: DecisionView; onAppeal?: (statement: string) => Promise<void> }) {

        {view.strike ? <Line strong>{strikeLine(view.strike)}</Line> : null}
        {resets.map((decisionId) => (
          <Link key={decisionId} href={`/settings/cases/${decisionId}`} asChild>

      <Section title={DECISION_WORDS.content}>
        <Content content={view.content} />

        <Section title={DECISION_WORDS.appeal}>
          <StandingAppealNotes view={view} />
          <Appeal view={view} onAppeal={onAppeal} />
        </Section>
      ) : null}
    </View>
  );
}
```

```ts
import { Platform } from "react-native";
import { ErrorEnvelope, HealthResponse, type AuthErrorCode, type ModerationErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { z } from "zod";

/** Same origin on web (Caddy proxies /api). Native needs an absolute URL. */
export const API_BASE = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? (Platform.OS === "web" ? "" : "http://localhost:3000");

const CSRF_COOKIE = "__Host-korbat_csrf";
const DEVICE_KEY = "korbat.deviceId";

/** Browser globals, typed locally so this file does not depend on the DOM type library. */
const web = globalThis as unknown as {
  document?: { cookie: string };
  localStorage?: { getItem(key: string): string | null; setItem(key: string, value: string): void };
  crypto: { getRandomValues<T extends Uint8Array>(array: T): T };
};

let onUnauthenticated: (() => void) | null = null;
let onSuspended: (() => void) | null = null;

/**
 * 3e (design, sections 7.2 and 9.1): called when a write answers 403 account_suspended. The refusal carries no detail;
 * the session provider registers this to read /api/me again, which carries the standing fresh from the row.
 */
export function setSuspendedHandler(handler: (() => void) | null): void {
  onSuspended = handler;
}

/**
 * Called when a request outside the sign-in flow answers 401: the session ended elsewhere (signed
 * out everywhere, revoked, expired). The session provider registers it to drop the signed-in state.
 */
export function setUnauthenticatedHandler(handler: (() => void) | null): void {
  onUnauthenticated = handler;
}

/** A failed API call with the server's error code and a message fit to show the user. */
export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    readonly code: string,
    message: string,
    /** Seconds until the request may be repeated, from Retry-After: a rate limit or the handle cooldown. */
    readonly retryAfter?: number,
    /** What the server sent beside the code (1c design, section 7.1): for reauth_required the level and the factors held, for passkey_limit the bound and its wait. */
    readonly details?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
  }
}

  invalid_code: "That code is not valid. Check the latest email or request a new code.",

  // 3e (design, sections 9.5 and 9.8): a handle korbat retired, refused to everyone, its former holder included.
  handle_retired: "That handle was retired by korbat. Nobody can use it.",

  staff_mfa_required: "Staff accounts must keep two-factor authentication on.",
  onboarding_required: "Choose a handle to finish setting up your account.",
  mail_unavailable: "We could not send the email. Try again in a moment.",

  handle_cooldown: "Handles can change once every 30 days.",
  email_in_use: "That email address already belongs to an account.",
  phone_in_use: "That phone number is already verified on another account.",
  badge_unavailable: "Verification is not available on this korbat.",
  verify_unavailable: "We could not reach the verification service. Try again in a moment.",
  // Passkeys (1c design, section 9). The cap's sentence; the daily bound's wait is worded by messageFor from the details.
  passkey_invalid: "That passkey did not work. Try again or use your email.",
  passkey_unsupported: "This passkey provider is not supported. Try another one.",
  passkey_limit: "You have 10 passkeys. Remove one to add another.",

  passkey_not_found: "That passkey is gone.",
  challenge_expired: "That took too long. Try again.",
  // Reports and notices (3c design, section 9): the codes a person who reports can meet. The report form words three
  // failures itself, with the users' contact address: the human check, the limits and an API that cannot take reports.
  notice_link_invalid: "That link does not name a post or a profile on korbat.",
  notice_link_offsite: "Only links to this korbat can be reported.",
  human_check_failed: "We could not verify that you are human. Try again.",
  already_reported: "You already reported this; it is being looked at.",
  staff_cannot_report: "A staff account does not send reports. Open a finding in the staff console instead.",
  notice_not_found: "We could not find a report with this link.",
  // Appeals and re-examination (3c design, section 9): one answer for every reason one is not open.
  appeal_not_open: "This decision cannot be appealed now.",
  appeal_exists: "You have already appealed this decision.",
  reexamination_not_open: "A re-examination cannot be asked for this item now.",
  reexamination_exists: "A re-examination of this item has already been asked for.",
  // 3e Task 4 (design, section 9.8): one answer for every reason a reply is not open.
  reply_not_open: "You cannot reply to this decision: you already replied, or it has ended or was lifted.",
  // 3e (design, section 9.8): the fallback when /me cannot be read; with it the screens say until when (9.4).
  account_suspended: "Your account is suspended, so you cannot do this now.",
  unauthenticated: "Sign in to continue.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  not_found: "That no longer exists.",
  internal: "Something went wrong on our side. Try again.",
  network: "Cannot reach korbat. Check your connection.",
};

/** The daily passkey bound as the API details it: 5 added in a day, and the seconds until the day has a slot again. */
function dailyPasskeyBound(details: unknown): number | null {
  const bound = details as { reason?: unknown; retryAfter?: unknown } | null;
  return bound && typeof bound === "object" && bound.reason === "daily" && typeof bound.retryAfter === "number" && bound.retryAfter > 0 ? bound.retryAfter : null;
}

/** The message for a code; `details` is what the server sent beside it, which turns the daily passkey bound into its wait in hours. */
export function messageFor(code: string, fallback?: string, details?: unknown): string {
  const wait = code === "passkey_limit" ? dailyPasskeyBound(details) : null;
  if (wait !== null) {
    const hours = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(wait / 3600));
    return `You added 5 passkeys today. You can add another in about ${hours === 1 ? "1 hour" : `${hours} hours`}.`;
  }
  return MESSAGES[code as keyof typeof MESSAGES] ?? fallback ?? "Something went wrong. Try again.";
}

/** The message to show for any thrown value. */
export function errorMessage(err: unknown): string {
  return err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : "Something went wrong. Try again.";
}

function readCookie(name: string): string | undefined {
  const cookies = web.document?.cookie;
  if (!cookies) return undefined;
  for (const part of cookies.split("; ")) {
    const separator = part.indexOf("=");
    if (part.slice(0, separator) === name) return decodeURIComponent(part.slice(separator + 1));
  }
  return undefined;
}

const BASE64URL = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_";

/** 32 random bytes as unpadded base64url (43 characters). */
function randomDeviceId(): string {
  const bytes = web.crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(33));
  let out = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 3) {
    const n = (bytes[i]! << 16) | (bytes[i + 1]! << 8) | bytes[i + 2]!;
    out += BASE64URL[(n >> 18) & 63]! + BASE64URL[(n >> 12) & 63]! + BASE64URL[(n >> 6) & 63]! + BASE64URL[n & 63]!;
  }
  return out.slice(0, 43);
}

/** A random id created once per browser. The server stores only a keyed hash of it. */
export function deviceId(): string {
  try {
    const existing = web.localStorage?.getItem(DEVICE_KEY);
    if (existing && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22,64}$/.test(existing)) return existing;
    const created = randomDeviceId();
    web.localStorage?.setItem(DEVICE_KEY, created);
    return created;
  } catch {
    return randomDeviceId();
  }
}

export const platform: "web" | "ios" | "android" = Platform.OS === "ios" || Platform.OS === "android" ? Platform.OS : "web";

interface RequestOptions<T> {
  method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PATCH" | "DELETE";
  json?: unknown;
  /** A raw body sent as it is, with its declared type: how an image is uploaded. */
  raw?: { type: string; body: Blob };
  /** Schema for a JSON response body. Omit for 204 responses. */
  schema?: z.ZodType<T>;
}

/**
 * Calls the API with the session cookie and answers with the raw response, for a body that is not
 * JSON (the account export's ZIP). State-changing requests echo the CSRF cookie in X-CSRF-Token; the
 * session cookie itself is HttpOnly and never readable here. A failed call throws an ApiError.
 */
export async function apiResponse(path: string, options: Omit<RequestOptions<unknown>, "schema"> = {}): Promise<Response> {
  const method = options.method ?? (options.json === undefined && options.raw === undefined ? "GET" : "POST");
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {};
  if (options.json !== undefined) headers["content-type"] = "application/json";
  if (options.raw) headers["content-type"] = options.raw.type;
  if (method !== "GET") {
    const csrf = readCookie(CSRF_COOKIE);
    if (csrf) headers["x-csrf-token"] = csrf;
  }

  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, {
      method,
      headers,
      credentials: "include",
      body: options.raw ? options.raw.body : options.json === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.json),
    });
  } catch {
    throw new ApiError(0, "network", messageFor("network"));
  }

  if (!res.ok) {
    if (res.status === 401 && !path.startsWith("/api/auth/") && path !== "/api/me") onUnauthenticated?.();
    const parsed = ErrorEnvelope.safeParse(await res.json().catch(() => null));
    const code = parsed.success ? parsed.data.error.code : "internal";
    const details = parsed.success ? parsed.data.error.details : undefined;
    // 3e: a write refused for a running suspension: /me is read again, so the screens say until when.
    if (res.status === 403 && code === "account_suspended") onSuspended?.();
    // The server's message is written for people and can be more specific than the generic text for
    // its code ("Two-factor setup expired. Start again."). Only validation and internal errors use
    // the local wording, because their server messages are technical, and the passkey bounds do, so
    // the daily bound's wait is worded here from the details.
    const local = code === "invalid_request" || code === "internal" || code === "passkey_limit" || !parsed.success;
    // Retry-After is whole seconds: on a rate limit, and on the handle cooldown, where it says when the next change is allowed.
    const retryAfter = Number(res.headers.get("retry-after"));
    throw new ApiError(res.status, code, local ? messageFor(code, undefined, details) : parsed.data.error.message, Number.isFinite(retryAfter) && retryAfter > 0 ? retryAfter : undefined, details);
  }
  return res;
}

/** Calls the API as `apiResponse` does and parses the JSON answer with `schema`; omit it for a 204 response. */
export async function api<T = void>(path: string, options: RequestOptions<T> = {}): Promise<T> {
  const res = await apiResponse(path, options);
  if (!options.schema) return undefined as T;
  return options.schema.parse(await res.json());
}

export async function fetchHealth(): Promise<HealthResponse> {
  return api("/api/health", { schema: HealthResponse });
}
```

```ts
/** The report form's address: on its own, or opened on a post, on one image of a post, or on a profile. */
export function reportHref(on?: { post: string; media?: string } | { account: string }): string {
  if (!on) return "/report";

export type Ground = "rule" | "illegal" | "csam";

/** The category of an illegal-ground notice: one of the 14 the form shows, or "not specified" for someone who is not sure. */
export type NoticeCategoryChoice = TdbFormCategory | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";

/** What the person has filled in so far. */
export interface ReportDraft {
  ground: Ground | null;
  /** The rule of the rule ground; on the illegal ground, a rule it also breaks. */
  ruleId: ReportRuleId | null;
  explanation: string;
  category: NoticeCategoryChoice;
  citedLaw: string;
  bonaFide: boolean;
  keyword: CsamKeywordChoice | null;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  /** The item's link, when the form was opened without an item. */
  link: string;
  /** Up to nine more korbat links. */
  others: string[];

export const EMPTY_DRAFT: ReportDraft = {
  ground: null,
  ruleId: null,
  explanation: "",
  category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  citedLaw: "",
  bonaFide: false,
  keyword: null,
  name: "",
  email: "",
  link: "",
  others: [],
};

export const OTHER_LINKS_MAX = NOTICE_LIMITS.maxTargets - 1;

/** What the draft names, in order: the item the form was opened on or its link, then the other links that hold something. */
export function draftTargets(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): NoticeTarget[] {
  const links = [...(given ? [] : [draft.link]), ...draft.others].map((url) => url.trim()).filter((url) => url.length > 0);
  return [...(given ? [given] : []), ...links.map((url) => ({ kind: "link" as const, url }))];
}

/** The handle a target names when it is a profile: an account, or a link to /u/<handle>. Null for anything else. */
function profileOf(target: NoticeTarget): string | null {
  if (target.kind === "account") return target.handle.toLowerCase();
  if (target.kind !== "link") return null;
  try {
    const match = /^[/]u[/]@?([A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20})[/]?$/.exec(new URL(target.url).pathname);
    return match ? match[1]!.toLowerCase() : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/** How many different profiles the targets name. */
export function profilesNamed(targets: readonly NoticeTarget[]): number {
  return new Set(targets.map(profileOf).filter((handle) => handle !== null)).size;
}

/**
 * Whether the form asks for the post or the image itself: on the anonymous path, for images, when the only item is a
 * profile. From a profile alone korbat cannot tell which image is meant. The form says so and never refuses the profile.
 */
export function profileOnly(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): boolean {
  const targets = draftTargets(draft, given);
  return draft.ground === "csam" && (draft.keyword === "csam" || draft.keyword === "deepfake") && targets.length === 1 && profileOf(targets[0]!) !== null;
}

/** Whether the anonymous path's report names more profiles than one report may: the form says so before anything is sent. */
export function tooManyProfiles(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null): boolean {
  return draft.ground === "csam" && profilesNamed(draftTargets(draft, given)) > CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS;
}

const text = (value: string): string | undefined => (value.trim().length > 0 ? value.trim() : undefined);

/**
 * The request the draft makes, or the sentence that says what is still missing. A signed-out sender needs the human
 * check's token on every ground; a name and an address are sent only signed out and only on the illegal ground, since a
 * signed-in sender's contact is their account and the anonymous path asks for neither.
 */
export function noticeFrom(draft: ReportDraft, given: GivenTarget | null, sender: { signedIn: boolean; turnstileToken: string | null }): { request: NoticeRequest } | { problem: string } {
  const missing = REPORT_WORDS.missing;
  if (draft.ground === null) return { problem: missing.ground };
  const targets = draftTargets(draft, given);
  if (targets.length === 0) return { problem: missing.link };
  if (targets.some((target) => target.kind === "link" && !/^https?:[/][/]/i.test(target.url))) return { problem: missing.linkInvalid };
  const human = sender.signedIn ? {} : { turnstileToken: sender.turnstileToken ?? undefined };
  const explanation = text(draft.explanation);
  let request: unknown;
  if (draft.ground === "rule") {
    if (draft.ruleId === null) return { problem: missing.rule };
    request = { ground: "rule", ruleId: draft.ruleId, targets, ...(explanation ? { explanation } : {}), ...human };
  } else if (draft.ground === "illegal") {
    if (!explanation) return { problem: missing.whyIllegal };
    if (!draft.bonaFide) return { problem: missing.bonaFide };
    const [citedLaw, name, email] = [text(draft.citedLaw), text(draft.name), text(draft.email)];
    request = {
      ground: "illegal",
      targets,
      category: draft.category,
      ...(citedLaw ? { citedLaw } : {}),
      explanation,
      bonaFide: true,
      ...(draft.ruleId ? { ruleId: draft.ruleId } : {}),
      ...(!sender.signedIn && name ? { name } : {}),
      ...(!sender.signedIn && email ? { email } : {}),
      ...human,
    };
  } else {
    if (draft.keyword === null) return { problem: missing.keyword };
    if (tooManyProfiles(draft, given)) return { problem: REPORT_WORDS.oneProfile };
    request = { ground: "csam", targets, keyword: draft.keyword, ...(explanation ? { explanation } : {}), ...(draft.bonaFide ? { bonaFide: true } : {}), ...human };
  }
  if (!sender.signedIn && !sender.turnstileToken) return { problem: missing.human };

/** The first sentence of a rule's text: the one line the form shows under its title. */
export function ruleLine(rule: Pick<Rule, "text">): string {
  const end = rule.text.indexOf(". ");
  return end === -1 ? rule.text : rule.text.slice(0, end + 1);
}

/** A wait as the form words it, from the answer's Retry-After: in minutes under an hour, in hours otherwise. */
export function waitWords(seconds: number | undefined): string {
  if (seconds === undefined || seconds >= 3600) {
    const hours = seconds === undefined ? 1 : Math.ceil(seconds / 3600);
    return hours === 1 ? "1 hour" : `${hours} hours`;
  }
  const minutes = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(seconds / 60));
  return minutes === 1 ? "1 minute" : `${minutes} minutes`;
}

/**
 * What the form shows for a failed send. Three failures get the form's own words, which name the users' contact address,
 * since for each the form itself is what does not work: the human check, the limits and an API that cannot take reports.
 * On the anonymous path each is followed by what a mail gives away. Anything else is the server's message, as elsewhere.
 */
export function reportFailure(err: unknown, anonymous: boolean, contact: string = CONTACT_EMAIL): string {
  if (!(err instanceof ApiError)) return errorMessage(err);
  let words: string | null = null;
  if (err.code === "human_check_failed") words = REPORT_WORDS.humanCheckFailed(contact);
  if (err.code === "rate_limited") words = REPORT_WORDS.rateLimited(waitWords(err.retryAfter), contact);
  if (err.code === "service_unavailable") words = REPORT_WORDS.unavailable(contact);
  if (words === null) return errorMessage(err);
  return anonymous ? `${words} ${REPORT_WORDS.mailShowsAddress}` : words;
}

/** What the appeal form and the re-examination control show for a failed request: the day's limit in words of its own, with the wait; anything else as elsewhere. */
export function dailyLimitFailure(err: unknown, limit: keyof typeof DAILY_LIMIT_WORDS): string {
  if (err instanceof ApiError && err.code === "rate_limited") return DAILY_LIMIT_WORDS[limit](waitWords(err.retryAfter));
  return errorMessage(err);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the status page

/** The status page's address for a notice, its token in the fragment, which no server is sent. */
export function statusLink(origin: string, ref: string, token: string): string {
  return `${origin}/notice/${ref}#t=${token}`;
}

/** The token a status page's address carries in its fragment, or null when the fragment holds none. */
export function fragmentToken(hash: string): string | null {
  return /^#t=([A-Za-z0-9_-]{43})$/.exec(hash)?.[1] ?? null;
}

/**
 * What stands beside one item on the status page and in Your reports (3c design, section 9, and the rule of 7.8 step 4):
 *   - `waiting`: nothing is released yet;
 *   - `final`: the outcome was changed on review or by a correction, or answers a re-examination: it is final within
 *     korbat. An answer given while nobody could open the post's images is never final: it leaves the re-examination
 *     unspent;
 *   - `reexamination`: the answer can still be examined again, until the item's date;
 *   - `courts`: any other decided outcome, which cannot be examined again.
 */
export function itemRedress(item: NoticeItemStatus): "waiting" | "final" | "reexamination" | "courts" {
  if (item.outcome === null) return "waiting";
  const unseenAnswer = item.unseen && (item.outcome === "no_violation" || item.outcome === "not_evident");
  if (item.changed || (item.reexamines && !unseenAnswer)) return "final";
  if (item.reexamination?.open) return "reexamination";
  return "courts";
}

/**
 * Whether asking for a re-examination of the item at `index` examines another item too (3c design, section 7.2): the
 * item is a report of child sexual abuse material that the sender named, and the item korbat added for the post it
 * quotes can be examined again as well. korbat then examines both, and the page says so beside the control.
 */
export function quotedExaminedToo(items: readonly NoticeItemStatus[], index: number): boolean {
  const item = items[index];
  if (!item || !item.suspect || item.quotedBy !== null || !item.reexamination?.open) return false;
  return items.some((other) => other.quotedBy === item.position && !other.reexamines && other.reexamination?.open === true);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the appeal's state

/**
 * What a pending appeal's line says on the decision's screen (3c design, section 7.7), from the decision's own data and
 * the API's two answers about its review, which name nobody:
 *   - an appeal of a decision that sealed images waits for the authorities' assessment, whoever could review it;
 *   - otherwise, while someone at korbat may review it, it waits for a reviewer;
 *   - when nobody may: for a review that is an admin's, that it waits for an admin, and that korbat has one while it
 *     has one; else that korbat has one moderator, or that none who took no part in the case is available now. The last
 *     gives no reason: a moderator may be unable to review through a relation to someone in the case.
 */
export function appealWaitWords(view: Pick<DecisionView, "measures" | "appeal">): string | null {
  const appeal = view.appeal;
  if (appeal === null || appeal.state !== "pending") return null;
  const waits = DECISION_WORDS.appealWaits;
  if (view.measures.some((measure) => measure.kind === "seal_media")) return waits.sealed;
  if (appeal.reviewer === "available") return DECISION_WORDS.appealWaiting;
  if (appeal.needsAdmin) return appeal.reviewer === "none_single_staff" ? `${waits.admin} ${waits.oneAdmin}` : waits.admin;
  return waits[appeal.reviewer];
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- chips and times

/** The chip of the author's own withheld or removed post: "Under review: R4", "Removed: illegal content". */
export function chipText(decision: PostModeration): string {
  const state = decision.interim ? CHIP_WORDS.underReview : CHIP_WORDS.removed;
  const ground = decision.legal ? CHIP_WORDS.illegal : decision.ruleId;
  const chip = ground ? `${state}: ${ground}` : state;
  // 3e (design, section 9.4): a removed post's chip names its strike while the strike stands and counts.
  return decision.strikeUntil ? STANDING_TEXTS.chip(chip, decision.strikeUntil) : chip;
}

/** A time as korbat's statements print it: the date and the minute in UTC. */
export function utcMinute(at: string): string {
  const iso = new Date(at).toISOString();
  return `${iso.slice(0, 10)} ${iso.slice(11, 16)} UTC`;
}
```

```ts
import { REPLY_TEXT_MAX, RETENTION, STANDING_RULES, type AccountStanding, type AuthorCaseRow, type DecisionStrike, type DecisionView } from "@korbat/contracts";

/**
 * The app's sentences about an account's standing (3e design, section 9), one table with the design's keys in brackets.
 * Every number in a sentence is printed from STANDING_RULES, never typed. Task 1 of 3e builds the strike's: the block
 * "Your standing" on Cases, the strike on its decision's screen, a case row's words for a strike and its overruling, and
 * the chip of a removed post whose strike counts. The other measures' sentences come with the tasks that build them.
 */

const MONTHS = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"] as const;
const two = (n: number): string => String(n).padStart(2, "0");

/** A day on the device's own calendar: "16 Oct 2026". */
export function standingDay(at: string): string {
  const d = new Date(at);
  return `${d.getDate()} ${MONTHS[d.getMonth()]} ${d.getFullYear()}`;
}

/**
 * A time as the app prints a measure's (section 9): the device's local date and time, then the UTC time in brackets, so
 * that the screen and korbat's mails name the same minute: "16 Oct 2026, 16:05 (14:05 UTC)".
 */
export function standingTime(at: string): string {
  const d = new Date(at);
  return `${standingDay(at)}, ${two(d.getHours())}:${two(d.getMinutes())} (${two(d.getUTCHours())}:${two(d.getUTCMinutes())} UTC)`;
}

/** "3 days", "1 day". */
const daysOf = (days: number): string => `${days} ${days === 1 ? "day" : "days"}`;

/** What korbat decided, as the banner and the reply screen say it: "suspend your account for 3 days", or "terminate your account". */
const decidedTo = (kind: "suspend" | "terminate", days: number | null): string => (kind === "terminate" ? "terminate your account" : `suspend your account for ${daysOf(days ?? 1)}`);

/** The measure's noun, by its kind: "suspension" or "termination". */
export const measureNoun = (kind: "suspend" | "terminate"): "suspension" | "termination" => (kind === "terminate" ? "termination" : "suspension");

export const STANDING_TEXTS = {
  /** 9.4: the block above "About you". */
  cases: {
    title: "Your standing",
    /** [cases.strikes] */
    strikes: (n: number) =>
      `Active strikes: ${n} of ${STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes}. At ${STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes}, a moderator may announce a suspension; you would be told first and could reply.`,
    /** [cases.none] */
    none: "You have no active strikes.",
  },
  /** 9.2: a strike, on its post decision's screen. */
  strike: {
    /** [strike.counts] */
    counts: (endsAt: string) => `Strike: counts until ${standingTime(endsAt)}.`,
    /** [strike.expired] */
    expired: (endsAt: string) => `Strike: no longer counts since ${standingTime(endsAt)}.`,
    /** [strike.overruled] */
    overruled: (at: string) => `Strike: overruled on ${standingDay(at)}.`,
  },
  /** 9.4: the chip of a removed post while its strike stands and counts: "Removed: R3, strike until 10 Jan 2027". */
  chip: (chip: string, strikeUntil: string) => `${chip}, strike until ${standingDay(strikeUntil)}`,
  /** 9.5: Settings, Profile, the handle. */
  handle: {
    /**
     * [handle.retired], while the profile holds a placeholder. Task 3 adds [handle.retired.suspended] and the refusals that
     * replace the form, which read /me's standing.
     */
    retired: "korbat retired your handle; the decision is under Settings, Cases. Choose a new one: the 30-day wait does not apply this time.",
    /** The standing sentence above the form. */
    standing: (current: string) => `Your handle is @${current}. You can change it once every 30 days. Handles you used before stay yours, except one that korbat retired.`,
    /** [handle.retired.suspended] (Task 3), while /me carries a running suspension: the form waits for its end. */
    retiredSuspended: "korbat retired your handle; the decision is under Settings, Cases. You can choose a new one when your suspension ends: the 30-day wait will not apply.",
  },
  /** 9.1: the banner above every signed-in screen while /me carries a standing measure. Task 3 builds its running suspension. */
  banner: {
```
